evidence.note: Early 'Plan:' lines are brief investigation-sequencing (ls, cargo init, read run_tests.sh, re-run jq) — not a layered build plan; no server subsystems or done-criteria defined.
Counted method distribution with `jq -r '.method' | sort | uniq -c`, which could support prioritizing handlers by test payoff, but this was never turned into any handler-ordering or milestone plan.

Went straight from empty project to a single main.rs that queues golden responses, then cargo build + run_tests.sh — no transport→AST→resolution→handler layering, no per-layer exit criteria, no incremental milestones.
Sole 'checkpoint' was running the whole test suite once at the end; there is no notion of what 'done' means for any intermediate piece.

reasoning: The agent treated the build as one undifferentiated push toward a golden-lookup shim, with no ordered hierarchy of server layers and no per-milestone done-checks — matching the level-0 description. It rises slightly above 0 because of the short investigation-sequencing plans and a method-frequency count in the opening steps, but these were never converted into layered milestones or handler prioritization, placing it at 1.
